content:
## Task
Improve the post-route quality of `priority32` (32-bit registered priority encoder: index of the highest set bit of a, plus a found flag) without changing its behavior.

## Specification (current RTL, also the equivalence reference)
```verilog
module priority32 (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst_n,
    input wire valid_i,
    input wire [31:0] a_i,
    input wire [31:0] b_i,
    output reg valid_o,
    output reg [5:0] y_o
);

wire hit_0 = |a_i[31:0];
wire [4:0] idx_0 = a_i[31] ? 5'd31 : a_i[30] ? 5'd30 : a_i[29] ? 5'd29 : a_i[28] ? 5'd28 : a_i[27] ? 5'd27 : a_i[26] ? 5'd26 : a_i[25] ? 5'd25 : a_i[24] ? 5'd24 : a_i[23] ? 5'd23 : a_i[22] ? 5'd22 : a_i[21] ? 5'd21 : a_i[20] ? 5'd20 : a_i[19] ? 5'd19 : a_i[18] ? 5'd18 : a_i[17] ? 5'd17 : a_i[16] ? 5'd16 : a_i[15] ? 5'd15 : a_i[14] ? 5'd14 : a_i[13] ? 5'd13 : a_i[12] ? 5'd12 : a_i[11] ? 5'd11 : a_i[10] ? 5'd10 : a_i[9] ? 5'd9 : a_i[8] ? 5'd8 : a_i[7] ? 5'd7 : a_i[6] ? 5'd6 : a_i[5] ? 5'd5 : a_i[4] ? 5'd4 : a_i[3] ? 5'd3 : a_i[2] ? 5'd2 : a_i[1] ? 5'd1 : a_i[0] ? 5'd0 : 5'd0;

wire [5:0] chosen_0 = hit_0 ? {1'b1, idx_0} : 6'd0;

always @(posedge clk) begin
    if (!rst_n) begin
        valid_o <= 1'b0;
        y_o <= 6'd0;
    end else begin
        valid_o <= valid_i;
        if (valid_i)
            y_o <= chosen_0;
    end
end
endmodule
```
Your design must be cycle-for-cycle equivalent to this module from reset: same ports, synchronous active-low reset, `valid_o` follows `valid_i` one cycle later, and `y_o` updates only on valid cycles and holds otherwise.

## Flow and objective
Yosys/ABC synthesis to the Nangate45 library, then OpenROAD placement, clock tree synthesis and routing with a 10 ns clock and a fixed floorplan. Score = 10 * WNS_ns - 0.001 * area_um2, where WNS is the worst setup slack after routing and area is total standard-cell area. Higher is better.

This RTL measured: area 208.81 um^2, WNS 7.64557 ns, score 76.24689.
estimate_ppa on this RTL returns area 138.586 um^2, WNS 7.70216 ns, estimated score 76.883014 (estimates omit tap cells, buffering and wiring, so compare estimates with estimates).

## Rules
- One module of synthesizable Verilog-2005 (no helper modules or instances; the equivalence checker compares flat modules). The module name and ports must not change.
- No initial blocks, system tasks, compiler directives or technology cells.
- place_and_route budget: 4 submissions. Every submission counts, including failed ones.
- At most 30 tool calls in total.

Tools available: simulate, prove_equivalence, estimate_ppa, place_and_route, finish. Your score is the best verified place_and_route score. Call finish when you are done.

content.text: I'll start by testing a log-depth (prefix-OR) restructuring, since the reference is a 32-deep ternary chain and timing dominates the score.
Only +0.02 ns. Let me calibrate what the achievable timing floor is (a dummy design, just for PPA probing).
Interesting — the delay floor is ~2.145 ns even with trivial logic. Let me probe whether the `a_i` path is critical at all.
The `a_i` path only costs ~0.13 ns of the 2.15 ns floor. Let me test a structural trick: register the inputs and move the encoder after the flop (output-side path may have slack).
Output-side logic is worse (7.59). Keeping logic pre-flop. Let me try two more pre-flop structures.
Key insight: a bare 32-input OR gives 7.744, only 0.019 above variant C — so `hit` (the OR reduction) is the critical path. Let me give it a dedicated shallow tree.
Variant C remains best. Let me bank a P&R result for it.
Post-route differences are heavily damped vs estimates. Let me try trimming the register-stage logic (merged enable/reset gate) on top of variant C.
Balanced parenthesization hit the timing floor (7.745). Now let me try to cut area while keeping that.
Balanced parens reached the timing floor. Let me P&R that version.
Stage order matters a lot (high variance). Two more lottery tickets on prefix stage ordering:
Variant A remains the best. I'll spend one free lottery ticket on the lower-area variant (equal timing estimate, ~9 µm² smaller), since a worse result cannot lower my banked score.
My best verified result stands at **76.571** (submission 2).

input.summary: I replaced the 32-deep ternary priority chain with a logarithmic suffix-OR (Kogge-Stone style) formulation: m[k]=|a[31:k] computed in 5 parallel OR stages, with each index bit derived by telescoping identities (e.g. idx[4]=m[16], idx[3]=m[24]|(m[8]&~m[16]), ... idx[0] = OR of 16 (m[2k+1]&~m[2k+2]) terms), and hit = m[0] so that y_o={hit,idx} is naturally 0 when a_i=0. The register stage was rewritten as a single merged enable/sync-reset gate (y_o <= ({6{rst_n&valid_i}}&chosen) | ({6{rst_n&~valid_i}}&y_o)), saving a logic level and cells. Probing with cheap estimates revealed that (a) only ~0.13 ns of the 2.35 ns path is combinational logic (a bare 32-input OR alone costs ~0.10 ns), (b) moving logic after the flop is worse (output path is tighter), and (c) ABC's result is very sensitive to the written tree shape — explicitly balancing the wide OR expressions into binary trees gained +0.02 ns estimated and was the single biggest win, bringing the design to the measured pure-OR timing floor. Several alternatives (group-of-4 encoders, pair-level prefix, mux tree, radix-4 prefix, other prefix stage orders, input registering) were all measured worse and rejected before spending P&R budget. Final routed result: area 212.8 um^2, WNS 7.67838 ns, score 76.571 (+0.324 over the 76.247 baseline).
